$comment: Hand-curated overrides on top of resorts.openskimap.json. Keys are resort ids. Every field in a resort entry is optional and replaces the OpenSkiMap value. Only add webcamUrl after checking the link opens.

exclude.high-wallowas: summer tramway, not a ski resort

revelstoke-mountain-resort.name: Revelstoke
revelstoke-mountain-resort.blurb: The longest lift-served vertical in North America (1,713 m), in the deep interior snowpack of BC's Selkirk Mountains. Big bowls and endless trees, with cat and heli skiing next door.

whistler-blackcomb.blurb: North America's largest ski area: two mountains and over 200 runs, linked by the Peak 2 Peak Gondola. Coastal storms bury the alpine, though the village can see rain.

kicking-horse-resort.name: Kicking Horse
kicking-horse-resort.blurb: Steep, big-vertical mountain above Golden, BC, packed with inbounds chutes and ridgelines. Dry Rockies–Purcells snow, and a gondola straight to the summit.

fernie-alpine-resort.name: Fernie
fernie-alpine-resort.blurb: Five big alpine bowls in the Lizard Range, which snags passing storms and averages about 9 m (30 ft) of snow a year.

whitewater-ski-resort.name: Whitewater
whitewater-ski-resort.blurb: Small, much-loved powder hill near Nelson, BC. About 12 m (40 ft) of snow a year, plenty of tree skiing and hardly any crowds.

lake-louise-ski-area.name: Lake Louise
lake-louise-ski-area.blurb: One of North America's largest ski areas, inside Banff National Park with views across to the Victoria Glacier. Cold, dry Rockies snow keeps the back bowls light.

big-sky-resort.name: Big Sky
big-sky-resort.blurb: Huge Montana resort topped by Lone Peak, with a tram to steep couloirs and a cold continental snowpack. Lift lines stay short for a mountain this size.

jackson-hole-mountain-resort.name: Jackson Hole
jackson-hole-mountain-resort.blurb: Legendary steeps off the Aerial Tram, including Corbet's Couloir, and 1,262 m (4,139 ft) of vertical. Teton storms regularly deliver big totals.

grand-targhee-resort.name: Grand Targhee
grand-targhee-resort.blurb: On the snowy west side of the Tetons, reached via Driggs, Idaho, averaging about 12.7 m (500 in) a year. Relaxed vibe, open glades, and cat skiing on neighbouring Peaked Mountain.

alta-ski-area.name: Alta
alta-ski-area.blurb: Skiers-only Utah classic at the top of Little Cottonwood Canyon, averaging over 13 m (500+ in) of light Wasatch powder a year.

snowbird.blurb: Steep, high-alpine terrain next door to Alta, served by a 125-passenger tram. The season often runs into late spring.

mammoth-mountain.name: Mammoth
mammoth-mountain.blurb: Tall volcano on California's Eastern Sierra with a 3,369 m (11,053 ft) summit and one of the longest seasons in the West. Sierra storms can drop huge multi-day totals.

palisades-tahoe-olympic-valley.name: Palisades Tahoe
palisades-tahoe-olympic-valley.blurb: Host of the 1960 Winter Olympics, on Lake Tahoe's north shore. Known for steep terrain like KT-22, and linked by gondola to Alpine Meadows.

kirkwood-mountain-resort.name: Kirkwood
kirkwood-mountain-resort.blurb: High on the Sierra crest south of Lake Tahoe, known for some of Tahoe's deepest snow and steepest terrain. Its elevation often turns other resorts' rain into snow here.

mt-baker.name: Mt. Baker
mt-baker.blurb: Holds the world record for measured snowfall in one season: 29 m (1,140 in) in 1998–99. Rugged, steep terrain and a laid-back, no-lodging vibe.

crystal-mountain.blurb: Washington's largest ski area, on the edge of Mount Rainier National Park. A gondola serves up Rainier views, with big lift-accessed backcountry terrain.

mt-bachelor.name: Mt. Bachelor
mt-bachelor.blurb: Big volcano in central Oregon's Cascades, with lifts to the summit and 360° skiing off the top. Drier than the coastal Cascades, with a long season.

steamboat-ski-resort.name: Steamboat
steamboat-ski-resort.blurb: Northwest Colorado resort famous for its trademarked "Champagne Powder" and some of the best aspen tree skiing in the Rockies.

wolf-creek-ski-area.name: Wolf Creek
wolf-creek-ski-area.blurb: Colorado's snowiest resort, averaging about 11 m (430 in) a year on the Continental Divide. No lodging on site, and often the first in the state to open.

taos-ski-valley.name: Taos
taos-ski-valley.blurb: Steep, high terrain in New Mexico's Sangre de Cristo Mountains, topped by Kachina Peak at 3,804 m (12,481 ft).
